summary: Single deployable monolith: Angular, Java + Spring Boot, PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted) database on Self-managed Linux servers (on-premise). It keeps data in Indian regions, matches the team's languages and is estimated at $0-$47 per month.

architecture.name: monolith
architecture.justification: One deployable is the fastest to build and simplest to run for a team of 5 and 0 feature areas (none).

alternatives.why_not: Adds service boundaries, network calls and per-service deployment that this team does not need at this scale (team 5).
Per-request functions suit light, spiky work; this backend runs as a long-lived service on Self-managed Linux servers (on-premise), which suits websockets, background jobs and steady traffic better.

frontend.justification: Angular matches the team's typescript skills; built-in XSS protections, long-term support.

alternatives.why_not: Nuxt scores 0.3 points lower overall, mainly on security (1.1 points).
Vue 3 + Vite (SPA) scores 0.3 points lower overall, mainly on security (1.3 points) and performance (0.5 points).

backend.justification: Java + Spring Boot matches the team's java skills; Spring Security, long audit history; is a proven choice for healthtech projects.

alternatives.why_not: Node.js + NestJS scores 0.3 points lower overall, mainly on security (0.9 points) and performance (0.5 points).
Node.js + Express scores 1.4 points lower overall, mainly on security (1.3 points) and maintainability (1.1 points).

database.choice: PostgreSQL, self-hosted on Self-managed Linux servers
database.justification: PostgreSQL is available in Indian cloud regions; carries HIPAA attestation; runs on your own host, as the deployment model requires; row-level security, mature auditing, encryption. It runs as PostgreSQL, self-hosted on Self-managed Linux servers; the team owns backups, patching and failover.

alternatives.why_not: MySQL (managed or self-hosted) scores 1.8 points lower overall, mainly on security (0.7 points).
Microsoft SQL Server / Azure SQL scores 2.6 points lower overall, mainly on vendor lock-in (0.8 points) and cost (0.7 points).

tradeoffs: Write scaling beyond one primary needs design
You run, patch and back up this database yourself on Self-managed Linux servers (on-premise).
database.offering: PostgreSQL, self-hosted on Self-managed Linux servers

hosting.justification: Self-managed Linux servers (on-premise) has Indian cloud regions; fits the air-gapped deployment model; offers a 99.95% SLA, in line with the 99.9% target; isolated network possible.

alternatives.why_not: Self-managed Kubernetes (on-premise) is a close second: only 0.0 points behind, with no single weakness.
Windows Server + IIS (self-hosted) scores 0.6 points lower overall, mainly on security (0.9 points) and performance (0.5 points).

tradeoffs: Needs real operations effort (patching, scaling, monitoring).

supporting.justification: Framework built-in auth (sessions/JWT): users sign in (email password); no external service; uses the backend framework's own session or token auth (Django auth, Laravel, ASP.NET Core Identity, Spring Security and similar); already part of the chosen core stack.

alternatives.why_not: A separate auth service (about $9-$19 per month, one more system to run) when Framework built-in auth (sessions/JWT) already covers this inside the core stack; worth it once the built-in option hits its limits. Score 0.69 vs 0.84.

tradeoffs: Password storage, resets, MFA and account lockout are your responsibility

supporting.justification: Postfix (self-hosted mail relay): email and password sign-in needs verification and reset emails; open-source mail transfer agent that relays application mail through the organisation's own mail servers, with no external service; free at this scale.

alternatives.why_not: No other email service satisfies the hard constraints.

tradeoffs: Someone has to configure relaying, TLS and queue monitoring

supporting.justification: GitLab CI/CD: automated build and deploy for the team; integrated pipelines, self-managed option.

alternatives.why_not: A close second with a smaller fit to this stack; score 0.72 vs 0.73.

assumptions: Load estimate: peak about 10 requests/second and about 1.4M requests/month from 2K users in 12 months.
Usage-priced items are shown as a band (0.75x to 1.3x of the estimate) because load figures are order-of-magnitude.
Public list prices of each product, in USD, without taxes, committed-use discounts or developer time.
The 99.9% availability target doubles or adds redundancy for hosting and database where needed.

warnings.message: On-premise hosting has no provider attestation for HIPAA; you carry the audit evidence yourself.
HIPAA needs a signed business associate agreement with the host, database and every vendor that touches health data.

CERT-In directions (April 2022) apply to services used in India: enable logs on all systems, keep them for 180 days within India, sync clocks to an NTP source and report cyber incidents within 6 hours. Size log retention and storage for this.

assumptions: No extra inputs supplied; neutral defaults are used (learning appetite medium, lock-in tolerance medium, budget strictness firm, no hiring plan, no mobile preference).
No cache layer: about 10 requests/second and 2,000 users in 12 months are served directly by the database or BaaS.

robustness.summary: The same stack wins in 6 of 14 checks. It switches to Vue 3 + Vite (SPA) (frontend), Node.js + NestJS (backend) when cost counted twice as much, security counted half as much; and to Self-managed Kubernetes (on-premise) (hosting) when cost counted half as much, time to market counted half as much, performance counted twice as much, maintainability counted half as much, security counted twice as much; and to Nuxt (frontend), Node.js + NestJS (backend) when time to market counted twice as much.
